Yo, happy Wednesday. Hope you’re not still recovering from Black Friday madness. Things are *moving* out there, from orbital data centers to exploding lead azide. Let’s dive in.

**Money Talk**

- **SpaceX gets FCC nod for orbital data centers.**
  Elon Musk's crew just got the green light to launch 1 million AI-chip-equipped data center satellites. Amazon fought it, but the FCC said "send it." Get ready for truly global cloud computing, or maybe just more space junk. [S1][S50]
- **Nvidia leads tech sell-off as AI concerns return.**
  Jensen Huang's comeback rally fizzled, with Nvidia and other AI-linked stocks taking a hit. Investors are weighing AI spending against inflation and higher rates. Apparently, even infinite compute has its limits when the economy's tight. [S2][S9]
- **Anthropic’s IPO minted 5,100 paper millionaires.**
  Meanwhile, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is pushing back hard on rivals accusing him of wanting to surrender human free will to AI. Good timing, given that sudden wealth can make people do weird things – hopefully not building sentient paperclip maximizers. [S5][S16][S43]
- **US economy is "ripping" with 4.3% Q3 growth.**
  Wall Street might be fretting over the future of the AI boom, but the underlying US economy is actually booming, with Q3 GDP figures significantly upgraded. Hard to square that with market jitters, but hey, the data says we’re cooking. [S18][S20]
- **Trump's Thanksgiving tariffs target China, EU, and a dozen others.**
  Just in time for the holidays, expect more trade friction as Trump unveils new levies, citing manufacturing capacity concerns. Supply chain headaches incoming, again. Happy Thanksgiving, indeed. [S6][S67]

**World Lore**

- **Trump pushes Netanyahu on Gaza peace plan.**
  Presidential envoy Jared Kushner is reportedly nudging the Israeli PM to uphold commitments made to Donald Trump on a Gaza peace deal. Interesting timing, given Trump's apparent desperation for a Ukraine deal before Democrats grab Congress. [S17]
- **China’s anti-corruption campaign claims Shanghai chief.**
  Politburo member Chen Jining is the latest high-profile official to get swept up in Xi Jinping's never-ending anti-corruption drive. Nobody's safe, apparently. Just another day in the Party's quest for ideological purity. [S25]
- **Hungary-Ukraine ties reset with new PM.**
  Peter Magyar, Hungary's new PM, met with Zelenskyy to thaw the "frosty and hostile" relations of the Viktor Orban era. A much-needed diplomatic reboot for Kyiv, finally getting an ally instead of an obstructionist neighbor. [S31]
- **Spain’s Canary Islands hit by record migrant arrivals.**
  Over 2,000 migrants landed in one day, putting "unprecedented migration pressure" on the islands just as Spain heads into elections this weekend. Expect this to dominate headlines there, fueling local frustrations and political drama. [S32]
- **US Army detonates tons of lead azide in Iowa.**
  After delays and presidential intervention, the Army finally blew up 68 drums of unstable explosives in a controlled blast. Officials praised "mitigation efforts," but locals were evacuated and still waiting on rigorous testing for environmental impact. [S19][S22][S34][S46][S51]

**Tech Tea**

- **1Password confirms security incident, customer names leaked.**
  The password manager giant admits hackers accessed an employee account, snagging customer names and emails. They swear passwords are safe, but cue the phishing attempts. Time to update your 2FA, folks, and maybe don't reuse email addresses. [S39][S44][S47]
- **SpaceX gets FCC approval for 1 million orbital data center satellites.**
  Elon Musk’s "Starmind" initiative just got the green light to deploy AI-chip-equipped satellites. Google and Blue Origin are also in this space race, meaning the future of cloud computing is literally in orbit. [S1][S50]
- **Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei rejects "surrendering free will to AI" claims.**
  Amodei is pushing back hard on accusations from rivals that he favors letting AI take control. This hot debate is getting spicy, especially after Anthropic's recent IPO, where he basically told Axios they misread the room. [S16][S43]
- **Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang broke code of conduct amid sell-off.**
  As Nvidia's stocks dip, reports surface that Jensen Huang's actions may have violated company ethics. This could have "consequences" for corporate culture, and investors are already twitchy about AI spending. Not a good look when the market is already nervous. [S2][S23][S41]
- **New York bans AI chatbot toys for kids.**
  Citing "troubling safety failures" and risks to emotional development, NYC put a five-year ban on AI chatbot toys. Smart move, or stifling innovation? You decide, but your kids won't be chatting with their AI plushies this Christmas. [S45]

**Creator Szn**

- **Brands are adding "no-AI" clauses to creator deals.**
  Creators are happy about the sentiment, but the fine print matters: does "no-AI" mean no AI *tools* at all, or just no AI *generated* content? This is shaping up to be the next big battleground for digital authenticity. [S60]
- **The "clipping economy" is changing as platforms crack down.**
  The wild west of content clipping is getting regulated. Platforms are tightening rules, forcing creators to rethink how they manage and control their content. Expect more formal licensing and less ad-hoc re-editing, which might be a good thing. [S57]
- **Shoppers are using AI for holiday product research.**
  AI is officially in the Black Friday trenches, changing how consumers discover products. Marketers, if you're not adapting your strategy to meet AI-driven buying behavior, you're already behind. Your algorithms better be ready. [S58]
- **Brands prioritize new customer acquisition this holiday season.**
  Black Friday/Cyber Monday is less about loyalty and more about grabbing fresh eyeballs. Expect aggressive deals and campaigns from everyone from A-Frame Brands to Ritual as they chase those new sign-ups. [S56]
- **Jump-roping toy soldiers are accidentally taking over your FYP.**
  Holiday theme park performers posted AI-fan videos as an inside joke, and now it's gone viral. Proof that sometimes, the weirdest, most unpolished content wins the algorithm lottery. You can't script this stuff. [S53]

**Supply Lines**

- **UPS targets healthcare logistics with Smartways acquisition.**
  Big Brown is beefing up its healthcare delivery game by acquiring Smartways Logistics in Australia and New Zealand. Smart move to tap into a high-value, specialized sector down under, leveraging their global network. [S76][S78]
- **Ex-Convoy CEO Dan Lewis launches new $277M logistics startup.**
  Dan Lewis, formerly of the now-defunct Convoy, has emerged from stealth with a new logistics venture, backed by $277 million. The trucking tech space isn't dead yet, apparently – just waiting for the next big pivot. [S93][S94]
- **Amazon drone crashes in Michigan, FAA investigating.**
  An Amazon delivery drone hit a fiber-optic cable, tangled in a power line, and crashed onto a garage. Another reminder that last-mile automation has its... *ups* and downs. Maybe just stick to the vans for now. [S87][S88][S90][S91]
- **Descartes Spot platform automates freight quoting in seconds.**
  Logistics tech firm Descartes says its new platform can quote 90% of freight requests in under 30 seconds, combining carrier rates, schedules, and surcharges. Could be a game-changer for freight forwarders looking to cut down on manual bids. [S65]
- **Asia-US West Coast container spot rates drop below $8,000.**
  Good news for shippers: Trans-Pacific spot rates are slipping from peak highs after a tentative labor deal averted a major strike at LA-Long Beach ports. Still, trade policy uncertainty and carrier capacity cuts could keep them elevated. [S61]
- **Maersk warns of UK logistics bottlenecks amid global port congestion.**
  The Danish giant is flagging continued disruption across its UK and Ireland network. High import volumes combined with port and inland transport bottlenecks mean cargo backlogs are still very much a reality. Get ready for those holiday delivery delays. [S72]
- **P&G plans supply chain workforce cuts, citing automation.**
  Procter & Gamble is looking to cut as much as 30% of its product-supply headcount by 2030, driven by increasing automation. The robots are coming for logistics jobs too, so get those excel skills honed, human. [S70]

**Speed Round**

- US Army blew up tons of explosives in Iowa, EPA says "zero lead."
- Germany's 2027 budget is €561 billion and still not enough for everyone.
- Fairphone 6 Plus is $100 off, letting you fix your phone without breaking the bank.
- A fast-growing far-right party not even on the ballot is shaking up Spain's election.
- UK food inflation could hit 5% next year, thanks to energy costs and El Niño.
- Some airlines are playing favorites with air waybill liability terms for big forwarders.
- PETA is accusing PepsiCo of animal abuse in its sugar supply chain.
